description: NovaForge is a student team passionate about space technology, AI, and innovation. We are building the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer inspired by NASA Moon and Mars missions. Our team welcomes developers, designers, AI enthusiasts, storytellers, and researchers who enjoy teamwork and learning. Join us to build an engaging astronaut training experience.
summary:
OUTPOST – Moon & Mars Survival Simulator

OUTPOST is an interactive space exploration and resource management simulation designed to make STEM learning engaging and practical for students. It allows players to take the role of a mission commander and manage a lunar or Martian outpost while keeping a crew of four astronauts alive for a 10-day mission.

Players must balance essential resources such as oxygen, water, food, energy, materials, crew health, and radiation protection. They can construct and upgrade base modules, including solar power arrays, greenhouses, oxygen generators, and water recycling systems. The simulation also introduces engineering decisions and unexpected mission events that challenge players to make strategic choices with limited resources.

The project addresses the challenge by transforming complex space engineering trade-offs into an interactive learning experience. Through resource monitoring, decision-making, analytics, and mission achievements, students learn about sustainability, life-support systems, and the importance of engineering decisions in space exploration.
details:
OUTPOST – Moon & Mars Survival Simulator

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

OUTPOST is an interactive space exploration and resource management simulation that allows students to experience the challenges of establishing and maintaining a human outpost on the Moon or Mars.

Players take the role of a mission commander responsible for four astronauts over a 10-day mission. They must manage seven essential resources: Oxygen, Water, Food, Energy, Materials, Crew Health, and Radiation Protection.

The application provides an interactive dashboard to monitor resource levels, daily consumption, production, and mission performance. Players can construct and upgrade infrastructure such as Solar Power Arrays, Greenhouses, Oxygen Generation Systems, Water Recycling Systems, Radiation Shielding, and Emergency Shelters.

The simulation also includes engineering decision scenarios, unexpected mission events, achievements, resource analytics, and a final mission performance report. Every decision has consequences, encouraging players to balance competing requirements with limited resources.

2. What are the benefits of the project?

  • Makes space science and engineering concepts easier to understand through practical interaction.
  • Develops critical thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
  • Introduces resource conservation and sustainable living concepts.
  • Demonstrates the importance of life-support systems, renewable energy, food production, and radiation protection.
  • Encourages students to learn through experimentation rather than only theoretical explanations.
  • Provides immediate feedback through resource indicators, analytics, warnings, and mission results.

3. What is the intended impact?

The intended impact is to make STEM education more interactive, engaging, and accessible.

OUTPOST helps students understand that space exploration involves complex engineering challenges and that every resource and decision matters. It encourages scientific curiosity and develops an understanding of sustainability, systems thinking, and engineering trade-offs.

The project can serve as an educational tool for students interested in space science, environmental sustainability, engineering, and technology.

4. What tools, programming languages, and software were used?

The project was developed using the following technologies:

  • React: To build the interactive user interface and application components.
  • TypeScript: To implement simulation logic, resource calculations, and structured data handling.
  • Vite: To provide the development environment and application build process.
  • Tailwind CSS: To style the application and create its responsive, space-themed interface.
  • Recharts: To visualize resource trends, consumption, and mission analytics.
  • Lucide React: To provide icons throughout the application.
  • Browser LocalStorage: To save and retrieve mission progress in the browser.
  • Visual Studio Code: For development and code management.

No specialized hardware is required. The application runs in a modern web browser on a computer.

5. How is the project creative and innovative?

The creativity of OUTPOST comes from combining space exploration, resource management, engineering decisions, and educational gameplay into one interactive simulation.

Instead of presenting students with fixed scientific information, the application allows them to experiment with different strategies and observe the consequences.

For example, building an Oxygen Generation System improves oxygen production but consumes energy. Constructing a Greenhouse supports food production and contributes oxygen, but requires electrical power. Installing radiation shielding improves crew protection but uses limited construction materials.

The Moon and Mars missions also provide different environmental conditions and challenges. Random mission events introduce uncertainty, making every playthrough an opportunity to explore different solutions.

6. What factors did we consider during development?

The following factors guided the design and development:

  • Resource sustainability: Ensuring players understand the balance between consumption and production.
  • Crew safety: Prioritizing oxygen, water, food, health, and radiation protection.
  • Engineering trade-offs: Making sure construction and decisions involve both benefits and costs.
  • Environmental differences: Representing the different conditions of the Moon and Mars.
  • Educational value: Connecting gameplay mechanics with real scientific and engineering concepts.
  • User experience: Designing an intuitive interface with clear indicators, visualizations, and feedback.
  • Replayability: Including multiple decisions, random events, upgrades, and achievements to encourage repeated exploration.
  • Accessibility: Making the simulation easy to operate without requiring specialized hardware or advanced technical knowledge.

Overall, OUTPOST combines interactive simulation and STEM learning to help students explore the engineering challenges of sustaining human life beyond Earth.
